assessments.reasoning: The English Government of Canada capture matches the claimed SHA-256. The grant and provider definition establish the character of the instrument. Versioning at [17577,17638) identifies the edition independently of page title, URL or modification date.

The repository’s pinned admission table at [533,942) covers an identifiable grant supported by a controlling source. The Canadian grant for information resources fits that classification. The scope document establishes the rule, while an actual active selection would need a registry record.

challenge.method: Applied SCES §§1 and 3 by checking whether the unversioned URL, page creator, language selector or shared v2.0 number could misidentify the edition or grantor. Compared the Canadian definitions and governing law with the UK originals and the SPDX plain text.
challenge.results: The body supplies the edition missing from the URL. English language metadata, the Canadian title, Ontario and Canadian governing law, and a separately labelled French link identify the representation. The provider granting rights is defined as “His Majesty the King in right of Canada.” The pinned SPDX plain text says “Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada.” Both expressly declare Canadian v2.0.

limitations: The English page links a separate French representation. Its versioning clause ties use to terms in force on the access date. Work-specific rights, redistribution and installation require separate evidence. Active is the intended Index state, and actual admission was outside scope.
reasoning: The Government of Canada publishes the English instrument on open.canada.ca. Creator metadata identifies the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat. The Versioning paragraph explicitly names Open Government Licence – Canada version 2.0. The Information Provider grants conditional use of covered information resources. This supplies the grant, identifiable text, edition and controlling source required by the Index license criterion.
